claim.pdf_says: c. Level-number 88 is assigned to entries which define condition-names associated with a conditional variable and can be used only as described by format 3 of the data description entry. (See page VI-20, The Data Description Entry.)
claim.markdown_says: c. Level-number 88 is assigned to entries which define condition-names associated with a conditional variable and can be used only as described by format 3 of the data description entry. (See page VI-20, The Data Description Entry.)
claim.why_it_matters: In the PDF the level-2 box drawn around general rule (2)b also encloses item c (the box closes after 'Entry.)' of item c); the markdown marks only item b with the box delimiters, so level-88 condition-names lose their Nucleus level-2 marking.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 257 (VI-25) shows a single rectangle whose top edge is above 'b. Level-number 66' and whose bottom edge closes under 'Entry.)' at the end of item c, so both items b and c of 5.7.4 GR(2) are level-2 (boxed) text. This matches the boxed '66, or 88.' in syntax rules (2) and (3) and the boxed 'condition-names' in 5.7.1. The markdown wraps only item b in the box delimiters (the closing marker follows b's 'Entry.)') and leaves item c unmarked. The words of item c are identical in both sources; the defect is the missing level-2 marking on item c.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim is accurate: in 5.7.4 GR(2) the PDF's level-2 box encloses items b and c together; the markdown closes the box after item b, so item c (level-number 88) loses its Nucleus level-2 marking. Text is otherwise identical.
